authority: Declared by ledger Entry 75 (carousel_method.json deferred_procedure) to run when the career clock passes February 2, 2014. User instruction of September 29, 2026: before advancing to February 17, assess whether any Jacksonville coach or coordinator is poached, looking into 2013 and resolving everything that can be resolved. This procedure therefore also resolves the part Entry 75 left unmodelled: coordinator openings at clubs that kept their head coach.
rules_source: library/2014_coaching_hiring_and_anti_tampering_rules.md section 8, as in Entry 75. Jacksonville's staff is past its season: head-coach requests cannot be refused; every other request is lateral and follows Jacksonville's standing default policy (grant a position coach's move to coordinator, refuse a move to the same job elsewhere).
window: Retroactive from January 12, 2014 (the day after Jacksonville's elimination) through February 17, 2014, the advance date. Anything decided after February 17 is recorded as pending and resolved when the clock passes it.
candidates: Jacksonville's eleven assistants under contract (career/2013/coaching_staff.md). Alan Lowry left on January 12 (Entry 75) and is not a candidate. Charlie Skalaski is not a coordinator candidate (Entry 75 method).

stage_D1_super_bowl_clubs.rule: Buffalo (Doug Marrone, first season, won Super Bowl XLVIII) and Minnesota (Leslie Frazier, third season, lost it) each change head coach with the probability of the base-rate cell already recorded for them in carousel_results.json (playoffs|1st season 0.0416; playoffs|2nd-3rd 0.0254). The vacancy opens February 3, 2014; the hire day is drawn from the January 2013 cycle's hire days as in Entry 75 (3, 6, 7, 9, 14, 15, 15, 16 days after the opening).
stage_D1_super_bowl_clubs.if_changed: Head-coach requests for Romeo Crennel and Mike Tice with Entry 75's head-coach request model (base 0.0604 times the normalized role, play-calling, club and unit factors; offer 0.5 / 5.8); granted, because Jacksonville's season is over. The new head coach then opens offensive coordinator (1.0) and defensive coordinator (0.875) jobs closing 2 to 10 days after the hire, with Entry 75's coordinator request model (base 0.0125 times the coach factor times the normalized club factor 1.5 / 1.1875; offer 0.25) and same-position requests at 0.03 (refused by policy).

stage_D2_retained_head_coach_clubs.clubs: Every club that kept its head coach: all 32 except Jacksonville, the five clubs that changed in Entry 75 (Atlanta, Cincinnati, Denver, Indianapolis, San Francisco) and Buffalo or Minnesota if they change in stage D1.
stage_D2_retained_head_coach_clubs.opening_rates: Per club, an offensive coordinator opening with probability 5/24 and a defensive coordinator opening with probability 4/24: in the January 2013 cycle, 24 clubs kept their head coach and opened 5 offensive and 4 defensive coordinator jobs (Carolina, Denver, Indianapolis, New York Jets and Oakland on offense; Dallas, Seattle, New Orleans and St. Louis on defense; interim coordinators made permanent at Baltimore and Tennessee are not openings). Source: the two-pass research recorded in library/2014_coaching_hiring_and_anti_tampering_rules.md's companion note career/2014/offseason/staff_changes/2013_retained_club_coordinator_turnover.md. Special teams coordinator openings (8 of 24 in 2013) are recorded but cannot reach Jacksonville's staff: Jacksonville has no special teams assistant and its coordinator job is itself vacant.
stage_D2_retained_head_coach_clubs.decision_dates: Each opening's decision date is drawn uniformly from the nine 2013 retained-club coordinator hire dates, moved to 2014: January 11, 17, 17, 18, 18, 18, 18, February 9, February 12. A search decided on January 11 cannot reach Jacksonville's staff (no request before elimination for a lateral or coordinator job, rule W10; no hire before elimination, rule X1).
stage_D2_retained_head_coach_clubs.requests: A Jacksonville candidate is asked on the later of January 12 and three days before the decision date, with probability 0.0125 times his coach factor (Entry 75: Bates 8, Bush 6, Yarno and Oden 1.5, Pleasant, Drake, Spencer, Zernhelt 1; Crennel and Tice 1.6 for the same job laterally) times the normalized playoff-club factor (1.5 / 1.1875).
stage_D2_retained_head_coach_clubs.offer: 0.0588 per interviewed sitting position coach. In the 2013 cycle only 2 of 17 coordinator openings at retained-head-coach clubs went to another club's sitting position coach (Tim Walton, Detroit secondary coach, to St. Louis; Keith Burns, Denver assistant special teams coach, to Washington): 0.118 per opening. Entry 75's new-staff model implies 160 x 0.0125 x 0.25 = 0.5 such hires per opening, so its 0.25 offer rate is scaled by 0.118 / 0.5. Retained clubs promote in-house or hire displaced and college coordinators far more often than new staffs do.
stage_D2_retained_head_coach_clubs.permission_and_acceptance: A position coach's move to coordinator is granted by Jacksonville's default policy and accepted (Entry 75 stage 5). A coordinator's move to the same job elsewhere is refused. One hire per club job.

draws: One private packet (this method's digest, the script's digest, the inputs' digest and the snapshot); one seeded generator makes every draw in a fixed structural order: stage D1 for Buffalo then Minnesota (change draw, hire-day draw, then every head-coach and coordinator request and offer draw whatever the dates); then stage D2 clubs in alphabetical order, offensive then defensive job (opening draw, decision-date draw, then a request and an offer draw for every candidate on that side). Events are applied in date order; a coach who has left is never asked again.
label_swap: Every probability reads only the job, the coach's role and record, the clubs' records and the calendar. The same method with any other employer gives the same probabilities for the same inputs.
